summary: The study describes the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of copper on carboxyl-terminated alkyl self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) to create top contacts for molecular electronic devices. The process uses copper di-sec-butylacetamidinate as a precursor and operates at 185 °C. The ALD method ensures the formation of a thin, non-damaging copper layer that protects the SAM layer, allowing for the deposition of a thicker metal top contact. The study confirms the chemical integrity of the SAM interface and the formation of a bidentate complex between copper and the COOH groups during the ALD process.
